O. HENRY · 30 TRUYỆN NGẮN · BÀI ĐỌC KÈM TỪ VỰNG

Hearts and Hands

Truyện 6 · Những quả tim và những bàn tay · 865 chữ · 53 từ

Từ in đậm được giải nghĩa ở cột bên phải. Chạm từ in đậm để tô sáng phần giải nghĩa. Mỗi truyện giải nghĩa độc lập.

BÀI ĐỌC
TỪ VỰNG

At Denver there was an influx of passengers into the coaches on the eastbound B. & M. express. In one coach there sat a very pretty young woman dressed in elegant taste and surrounded by all the luxurious comforts of an experienced traveler. Among the newcomers were two young men, one of handsome presence with a bold, frank countenance and manner; the other a ruffled, glum-faced person, heavily built and roughly dressed. The two were handcuffed together.

  • influx (n) /ˈɪnflʌks/dòng người đổ vào
  • eastbound (adj) /ˈiːstbaʊnd/đi về hướng đông
  • B. & M. express (cụm từ)chuyến tàu tốc hành của hãng đường sắt Burlington & Missouri
  • presence (n) /ˈprezns/nghĩa trong bài: dáng vẻ, phong thái
  • frank (adj) /fræŋk/cởi mở, thẳng thắn
  • countenance (n) /ˈkaʊntənəns/nét mặt, vẻ mặt
  • ruffled (adj) /ˈrʌfld/xộc xệch, nhàu nhĩ
  • glum-faced (adj) /ˈɡlʌm feɪst/mặt mày cau có, ủ ê
  • heavily built (cụm từ)to con, vạm vỡ
  • handcuff (v) /ˈhændkʌf/còng tay

As they passed down the aisle of the coach the only vacant seat offered was a reversed one facing the attractive young woman. Here the linked couple seated themselves. The young woman’s glance fell upon them with a distant, swift disinterest; then with a lovely smile brightening her countenance and a tender pink tingeing her rounded cheeks, she held out a little gray-gloved hand. When she spoke her voice, full, sweet, and deliberate, proclaimed that its owner was accustomed to speak and be heard.

“Well, Mr. Easton, if you will make me speak first, I suppose I must. Don’t you ever recognize old friends when you meet them in the West?”

  • aisle (n) /aɪl/lối đi giữa các hàng ghế
  • reversed (adj) /rɪˈvɜːst/quay ngược chiều (ghế quay mặt về phía sau tàu)
  • disinterest (n) /dɪsˈɪntrəst/sự thờ ơ
  • tinge (v) /tɪndʒ/nhuốm nhẹ (màu)
  • deliberate (adj) /dɪˈlɪbərət/thong thả, khoan thai
  • proclaim (v) /prəˈkleɪm/cho thấy rõ
  • accustomed to (cụm từ)quen với

The younger man roused himself sharply at the sound of her voice, seemed to struggle with a slight embarrassment which he threw off instantly, and then clasped her fingers with his left hand.

  • rouse oneself (cụm từ)bừng tỉnh, chú ý ngay
  • throw off (cụm động từ)gạt đi, rũ bỏ
  • clasp (v) /klɑːsp/nắm chặt

“It’s Miss Fairchild,” he said, with a smile. “I’ll ask you to excuse the other hand; it’s otherwise engaged just at present.”

  • otherwise engaged (cụm từ)đang bận việc khác (nói đùa)

He slightly raised his right hand, bound at the wrist by the shining “bracelet” to the left one of his companion. The glad look in the girl’s eyes slowly changed to a bewildered horror. The glow faded from her cheeks. Her lips parted in a vague, relaxing distress. Easton, with a little laugh, as if amused, was about to speak again when the other forestalled him. The glum-faced man had been watching the girl’s countenance with veiled glances from his keen, shrewd eyes.

  • bind (v) /baɪnd/buộc, trói
  • bracelet (n) /ˈbreɪslət/vòng đeo tay; ở đây (tiếng lóng) là chiếc còng
  • bewildered (adj) /bɪˈwɪldəd/hoang mang, bối rối
  • forestall (v) /fɔːˈstɔːl/chặn trước, nói trước
  • veiled (adj) /veɪld/kín đáo, che giấu
  • shrewd (adj) /ʃruːd/sắc sảo, tinh khôn

“You’ll excuse me for speaking, miss, but, I see you’re acquainted with the marshall here. If you’ll ask him to speak a word for me when we get to the pen he’ll do it, and it’ll make things easier for me there. He’s taking me to Leavenworth prison. It’s seven years for counterfeiting.”

“Oh!” said the girl, with a deep breath and returning color. “So that is what you are doing out here? A marshal!”

  • acquainted with (cụm từ)quen biết
  • marshal (n) /ˈmɑːʃl/cảnh sát tư pháp liên bang Mỹ, lo bắt giữ và áp giải tù
  • pen (n) /pen/(tiếng lóng) nhà tù, nói tắt của “penitentiary”
  • Leavenworth (n) /ˈlevənwɜːθ/nhà tù liên bang ở bang Kansas
  • counterfeiting (n) /ˈkaʊntəfɪtɪŋ/tội làm tiền giả

“My dear Miss Fairchild,” said Easton, calmly, “I had to do something. Money has a way of taking wings unto itself, and you know it takes money to keep step with our crowd in Washington. I saw this opening in the West, and—well, a marshalship isn’t quite as high a position as that of ambassador, but—”

  • take wings (cụm từ)(lời Kinh Thánh) tiền tự mọc cánh bay đi
  • keep step with (cụm từ)theo kịp, sánh bước cùng
  • crowd (n) /kraʊd/nghĩa trong bài: nhóm bạn bè cùng giới
  • opening (n) /ˈəʊpənɪŋ/nghĩa trong bài: cơ hội việc làm
  • marshalship (n) /ˈmɑːʃlʃɪp/chức marshal
  • ambassador (n) /æmˈbæsədə/đại sứ

“The ambassador,” said the girl, warmly, “doesn’t call any more. He needn’t ever have done so. You ought to know that. And so now you are one of these dashing Western heroes, and you ride and shoot and go into all kinds of dangers. That’s different from the Washington life. You have been missed from the old crowd.”

The girl’s eyes, fascinated, went back, widening a little, to rest upon the glittering handcuffs.

“Don’t you worry about them, miss,” said the other man. “All marshals handcuff themselves to their prisoners to keep them from getting away. Mr. Easton knows his business.”

“Will we see you again soon in Washington?” asked the girl.

  • call (v) /kɔːl/nghĩa trong bài: đến thăm (lối nói cũ)
  • dashing (adj) /ˈdæʃɪŋ/hào hoa, bảnh bao

“Not soon, I think,” said Easton. “My butterfly days are over, I fear.”

  • butterfly days (cụm từ)những ngày ăn chơi bay bướm

“I love the West,” said the girl irrelevantly. Her eyes were shining softly. She looked away out the car window. She began to speak truly and simply without the gloss of style and manner: “Mamma and I spent the summer in Denver. She went home a week ago because father was slightly ill. I could live and be happy in the West. I think the air here agrees with me. Money isn’t everything. But people always misunderstand things and remain stupid—”

  • irrelevantly (adv) /ɪˈreləvəntli/lạc đề, chẳng ăn nhập
  • gloss (n) /ɡlɒs/lớp hào nhoáng bề ngoài
  • agree with (cụm động từ)hợp với (sức khỏe) của tôi

“Say, Mr. Marshal,” growled the glum-faced man. “This isn’t quite fair. I’m needing a drink, and haven’t had a smoke all day. Haven’t you talked long enough? Take me in the smoker now, won’t you? I’m half dead for a pipe.”

The bound travelers rose to their feet, Easton with the same slow smile on his face.

  • growl (v) /ɡraʊl/gầm gừ, càu nhàu
  • smoker (n) /ˈsməʊkə/nghĩa trong bài: toa hút thuốc

“I can’t deny a petition for tobacco,” he said, lightly. “It’s the one friend of the unfortunate. Goodbye, Miss Fairchild. Duty calls, you know.” He held out his hand for a farewell.

  • petition (n) /pəˈtɪʃn/lời thỉnh cầu (chữ trang trọng, nói vui)
  • unfortunate (n) /ʌnˈfɔːtʃənət/người bất hạnh

“It’s too bad you are not going East,” she said, reclothing herself with manner and style. “But you must go on to Leavenworth, I suppose?”

“Yes,” said Easton, “I must go on to Leavenworth.”

  • reclothe (v) /ˌriːˈkləʊð/khoác lại. Ý: lấy lại vẻ khách sáo, kiểu cách

The two men sidled down the aisle into the smoker.

  • sidle (v) /ˈsaɪdl/đi lách nghiêng người

The two passengers in a seat nearby had heard most of the conversation. Said one of them: “That marshal’s a good sort of chap. Some of these Western fellows are all right.”

  • good sort (cụm từ)người tử tế, dễ mến

“Pretty young to hold an office like that, isn’t he?” asked the other.

  • hold an office (cụm từ)giữ một chức vụ

“Young!” exclaimed the first speaker, “why—Oh! didn’t you catch on? Say—did you ever know an officer to handcuff a prisoner to his right hand?”
